title: for loops, nested loops and loop design
learningObjectives: Use for loops with initialization, condition and iteration expressions.
Explain the order in which a for loop initializes, tests, executes and updates.
Design nested loops for rows, columns and repeated combinations.
Calculate iteration counts and recognize off-by-one errors.
Avoid modifying loop-control variables unexpectedly inside the loop body.

understand.concept: A for loop combines an initialization expression, a controlling condition and an iteration expression. Initialization runs once, the condition is checked before each iteration, and the iteration expression runs after the body before the next condition check. Nested loops place one loop inside another and are useful for tables, grids and repeated combinations.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding for loops, nested loops and loop design helps you reason about program behaviour instead of memorizing syntax. It is useful in exams, debugging and building reliable C applications.
understand.analogy: Treat the concept as a tool with a precise contract: it has valid inputs, defined operations and observable results.
understand.analogyLimit: An analogy is only an aid; the C standard and the relevant function specifications determine actual behaviour.

explain.narrative:
## 1. for loop structure

A for loop has the form `for (initialization; condition; iteration)`. Initialization runs once. The condition is tested before each body execution. The iteration expression runs after the body and before the next condition test.

## 2. Counted iteration

A common pattern initializes an index to zero, continues while it is less than a count, and increments it. For an array with count elements, indices run from zero through count minus one. Use a type appropriate for the count and index.

## 3. Nested loops

A nested loop executes the inner loop for each iteration of the outer loop. A row-and-column traversal commonly uses an outer row index and an inner column index. The total number of inner-body executions depends on both loop bounds.

## 4. Boundaries and progress

Test empty ranges, one element and the last valid index. Ensure the update moves toward termination and does not overflow. Avoid changing the loop variable unexpectedly in the body because it makes the iteration sequence harder to reason about.

## 5. Keep loop intent visible

Use meaningful index names and keep the loop condition simple. If the body performs several unrelated tasks, extract helper functions to make the iteration logic easier to understand.

questions.prompt: When does the iteration expression in a for loop run?
options: After the body and before the next condition test
Only when the condition is false
questions.answer: After the body and before the next condition test
questions.explanation: The iteration expression runs after each completed body execution.

questions.prompt: How many times does `for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i)` execute its body?
questions.explanation: The values of i are 0, 1, 2 and 3.

questions.prompt: What is a common purpose of nested loops?
options: Traversing rows and columns of a two-dimensional structure
questions.answer: Traversing rows and columns of a two-dimensional structure
questions.explanation: An outer loop can control rows and an inner loop can control columns.

questions.answer: A loop executes one too many or one too few iterations due to a boundary mistake

questions.prompt: Why should a loop-control variable not be changed unpredictably inside the body?
options: It makes the iteration sequence and termination harder to reason about

questions.answer: It makes the iteration sequence and termination harder to reason about
